Soccer. Under-tens, Saturday mornings at the park. Half the parents yell in Spanish, half in English. The kids ignore both equally.

Honestly? No. She got my mom into the English class at the library. Walked her over and stood there the whole first hour. $ [warm] And she told me my Spanglish is 'an asset.' Nobody has ever called it that. Don't tell her I said any of this.
Soccer fundraiser. I had to ask {homeLead} for the kitchen. You ask him something, he tells you a story about 1989, and then he says yes.

Not hard. It's just 'ours' with him, all the time. I'm the one with the school Spanish, so I'm the one who 'went to the library.' $ [warm] He still bought forty tamales for the team. Cash, no receipt. He's hard to stay mad at.
choice1: Forty tamales is a lot of support.

line: Shh, it's not coffee, it's 'a beverage.' Exam's Friday. I made two hundred flashcards and I'm on number forty.
Actually, would you quiz me? Ten minutes. You read the card, I panic, you say 'no' gently.
Metoprolol. _waits_ Okay, that one's easy. Propranolol. $ [warm] See, I know these. I actually know these. It's the clock that gets me.
choice2: Who taught you to study like this?
choice3: I should go. You've got this.

line: Nobody, really. My parents finished school at eighth grade, in Michoacán. They don't know what a flashcard is, but my dad checks every night that my lamp is on.
My mom asks if the teachers are nice. My dad asks if it pays. Honestly, both good questions.
Oh, hey. Did you get volunteered too? My mom signs me up for the pantry and tells me after.
choice1: I came on my own, actually.

line: Handing out bags, and reading the rules sheet out loud in Spanish for Mr. Funes. He reads it more carefully than anyone alive.
One bag per household. Bring ID if you have it, no ID is also fine. Every week Mr. Funes asks what counts as a household.
Whoever eats at your table. {homeLead} wrote that line. It's the best sentence in the building.
Always. Could you take the line for twenty minutes? I have to call my tía back or she'll call my mom.
_comes back with her phone_ Thank you. She wanted to know if I'm eating. I'm eating. She's going to call my mom anyway.
The week of an exam, no. Otherwise, kind of. Here nobody asks where I'm from, because they all know my mom. At school it's the first question.
choice3: I'll let you get back to it.

line: Hey, {playerName}. Can I ask you something weird? Not very weird. Medium.
My clinical instructor wants a page on why we chose nursing. Everyone's writing about a grandmother in a hospital bed. I don't want to write that.
The waiting room. Eight years old, my mom's purse on my lap, translating 'fasting' without knowing what it meant. $ [worried] Is that too much? I don't want it to sound like I'm asking for pity.
choice2: What did you tell her it meant?
choice3: I think it's good. I should go.

line: I told her not to eat for a week. _laughs_ She ate. She knew. Do you ever feel like the visiting team, wherever you are?
Huh. Okay. I think I'll write about the waiting room, then. Thanks for sitting through the medium-weird.
choice1: Send it to me when it's done.

line: Hey. Sorry, I'm not really studying. I've read this page four times.
Hey. Sorry, I've counted these pantry bags three times and I keep losing the number.
Nothing new. The news is just on in every room at home now. My dad turns it up, my mom turns it down.
choice3: That sounds stressful. I'll let you read.

line: He made us practise again last night, what to say if someone stops the car. My little brother laughed. My dad didn't.
choice3: I'm sorry. I'll let you be.

line: He got it. He's fifteen, he just didn't want to look scared in front of me. Anyway. Don't make the face. Quiz me on something.
Okay, you can't tell anyone yet, but I might have a job.
The clinic is hiring a part-time Spanish interpreter. Tuesday mornings. My clinical instructor asked if I'd thought about it.
Probably. It's funny, I've done it for free since I was eight. Now there's a form, and a badge, and a training on neutrality.
You're not supposed to add anything. Just say what the doctor says. $ My whole childhood I added things. 'She's scared, be nice to her.' I don't know if I can stop.
Pilar says you're at the hall every day now. Be careful.
{homeLead} says you're at the hall every day now. Careful.
He's going to ask you to sit with the young ones on Thursdays. He asked me once, for about a minute. Then he heard my Spanish and asked my cousin instead.
It's fine. My cousin talks less than me, he's better at meetings. $ [warm] Go, though. You'd be good at it. Bring a jacket, those Thursday meetings run till eleven and the heat goes off at nine.
The fiesta committee. She did it to me in 2019. I said yes to one meeting about napkins and I'm still on it.
No. It's nice, actually, don't tell her. My tía's on it too, and she's different there. Less 'how come you never call,' more 'carry this.'

Back table, with the nursing girls. You missed the one about the Rio Grande. I said nothing. I'm a good person.
You were not close. _grins_ So is it all library now, or do you still come to the hall?
That's fine. I was the same for a while. I went back for the soccer kids, not for me. Then it turned out it was kind of for me.

It's fine. I was loud, you were busy. Exam week, I get a little feral.
